data.text: [00:00]CD2 Track 35
I = Interviewer, S = Sarah

[00:04]Today, we’re talking about advertising. `[00:07.9]The aim of any company is to sell, and to continue to sell, more than other companies. `[00:14.4]And to keep ahead of the competition, companies need to advertise their product better and better in order to influence potential customers. `[00:23.5]Top advertising executive, Sarah Delaney, is with us today to talk about new developments in advertising and the amazing technological developments which make them possible. `[00:35.7]Good morning, Sarah.
[00:36.8]Hello.
[00:38]So ... , before we talk about these new developments, Sarah, can you tell us ... `[00:45.3]what kinds of adverts have the most influence on people?

[00:49.9]Well … , that’s an interesting question ... . `[00:52.2]Erm ... I think that all advertising has some kind of influence on people. `[00:57.7]I mean we may think, perhaps, that we make free choices about which products to buy, ... `[01:03.4]but actually, the adverts that you’ve seen will certainly influence what you think about different products ... `[01:10]even though you may not think about that consciously.
[01:13.1]Yes, adverts put ideas in your head, even if you don’t want them there! `[01:19]So, what do you think makes an advert effective? `[01:23.3]What are the most effective types of adverts?

[01:26.4]Erm ... the most effective types of adverts ... `[01:30.5]well ... , I think it depends really. `[01:33]Some people respond to humour; some people like an advert to have a lot of information; other people are very influenced by their favourite celebrity in an advert. `[01:44]I think in the end, adverts are effective because they are very clearly aimed at certain groups of people ... `[01:51.4]and a lot of research goes into which group of people your advert is aimed at.
[01:56]And it’s not just who the adverts are aimed at ... `[01:59.6]there is also a lot of research into how and where to advertise, isn’t there?
[02:05.5]Yes, and with new technological developments, things are changing all the time.
[02:11]So ... , what’s new in the advertising world, then?
[02:16]Well ... there’s one new innovation which means that television viewers may soon see adverts during their favourite documentary or drama series.
[02:27.6]Oh, really?

[02:29.5]Yes. `[02:30.4]Some developers for television companies are planning pop-up advertisements. `[02:36.4]That means logos or messages can be flashed up on the screen during a programme so the company doesn’t have to wait until the commercial break to advertise. `[02:48.3]Basically, the new technology is used to find a blank space on the screen to put the logo on – like some blue sky or a blank wall – you know, not covering someone’s face in your favourite soap opera.
[03:03.6]Even on a blank space, it sounds annoying!

[03:06.6]Well, yes – some people would say very annoying! `[03:11.3]Some people are worried that these pop-up adverts will destroy their enjoyment of a programme. `[03:17.5]The developers are convinced, however, that consumers will like them.
[03:22.7]I’m not sure they’re right about that! ...
[03:25.4]Well ... there are other developers who agree with you. `[03:29.5]In Japan, they are developing an approach which is very different ... `[03:34.8]almost the opposite really.
[03:36.7]Mmm ... ?

[03:37.7]Yes ... Nintendo has created a new internet video site for games consoles, and it uses a new system for advertising. `[03:49.3]The company did some research about the way customers are influenced by adverts and they decided they didn’t want to force viewers to watch adverts. `[04:00.2]With the new system, no adverts are shown on the screen at all. `[04:05.3]Consumers choose to watch adverts only if they want to.
[04:10]Ah! That sounds better!

[04:12.9]Mmm ... and if they do choose one, they get a very informative kind of advert … with more detailed and interesting information about the product. `[04:24.2]And as well as the advert itself, consumers can do other useful things, like receive vouchers to get discounts or even order some free samples of the product. `[04:37.2]The company hopes that adverts will change from something we avoid watching, to something we want to watch. `[04:45.6]They may even become one of the most popular things on TV, you never know, … these entertaining adverts may actually become a form of entertainment in themselves, in fact.
[04:57.4]Yes – that would really turn things around, wouldn’t it? `[05:00.8]Adverts either spoil your favourite show or they become your favourite show!
[05:06.3]That’s right! `[05:07.7]But you know, in whichever way companies choose to get their message across, one thing is for sure: advertising, in some form, is here to stay ...
